title: Female Reproductive System: Ovaries, Oviducts, & Coelomic Release
topic: Mesovarium, Independent Kidney Independence, Oviducal Ostium, & Spawns
topics: CRITICAL TRAP: Zero Anatomical Connection Between Ovaries and Kidneys
quickSummary: The female reproductive system consists of paired lobed ovaries suspended by the Mesovarium near the kidneys. Unlike males, the female ovaries have NO anatomical connection with the kidneys. Ripe ova rupture into the coelom, are swept into ciliated anterior oviduct funnels (Ostia), travel down coiled Oviducts, collect in Ovisacs, and discharge separately into the cloaca as gelatinous spawns (2,500–3,000 eggs).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### Primary Structures
• **Ovaries**: Paired large, thin-walled, irregular, lobed, dark structures situated near the kidneys, suspended by the **Mesovarium** peritoneal fold.
• **CRITICAL NEST TRAP**: The ovaries have **NO ANATOMICAL OR FUNCTIONAL CONNECTION WITH THE KIDNEYS**. Mature eggs break out of ovarian follicles directly into the body coelom.
• **Oviducts (Müllerian Ducts)**: Paired long, highly convoluted, white muscular tubes:
  - **Ostium (Oviducal Funnel)**: Wide ciliated funnel near the lungs that draws coelomic ova inward.
  - **Ovisacs**: Dilated posterior chambers where eggs are temporarily stored before passing into the cloaca.
• **Spawning**: A gravid female discharges **2,500 to 3,000 eggs** at a time in water enclosed in gelatinous protective egg masses called **Spawns**.
